about: The least memory each role needs resident on the device, as formulas over a model's shapes and the run's settings (workflow/min_memory.py evaluates them with tune's formula reader; no engine is named). Tensors are sorted by the one classifier (profile/roles.py): expert stacks, the output head, lookup tables (a step reads one row), unclassified (the classifier's 'other': unknown) and dense (the rest); their bytes are the header's (decode_roles._physical_bytes). Per architecture: meta = fact -> metadata key under the architecture's prefix (a per-layer list is one value only when its nonzero entries agree; else the fact is missing and the rows that read it are unknown); dims = fact -> [tensor pattern, axis]; counts = n_<fact> -> the pattern of one tensor per such layer; terms = named formulas over the facts, in order. Settings are facts: context, ubatch, draft_depth, and <x>_type as <x>_elem_bytes through the format registry. class: exact (the formula is the need, under the condition its `why` states) or bounded (a floor; `rest` says what sets the remainder). `every`: roles no model's shapes give, with the measurement that settles each. docs/context-audit.md, Minimum memory.

roles.copies: copies of the other file's tensors

every.test: the device's used memory after the runtime starts and before the first tensor, under each driver and runtime version: the least is the smallest seen
total - used - free off the device's samples (the audit's memory section) on each driver: what the device keeps for itself

terms.rs_ple: 0 if n_ple_layers == 0 else n_ple_layers * (ple_kernel - 1) * ple_ngram * streams * n_embd * state_elem_bytes
terms.rs_rollback: draft_depth * (n_recurrent_layers * (conv_width + 2 * rank) + (0 if n_ple_layers == 0 else n_ple_layers * streams * n_embd)) * state_elem_bytes

rows.why: every step multiplies by all of them
every step scores the whole vocabulary
a token reads one row of each: the device need not hold the table

rows.rest: a decode can run with every expert off the device, so nothing must be resident; what to keep is a speed choice, set by the cost of a step's experts off the device per byte and each expert's touch rate (a routing capture). One token reads experts_used of experts per layer (experts_one_token)

rows.why: a query may select any cell; keeping old cells off the device is a placement, judged by its measured fetch cost

rows.formula: n_indexer_layers * (ceil(context / pool) + pool - 1 + draft_depth) * idx_key_len * kv_elem_bytes
rows.why: the indexer scores one pooled key per pool; raw keys are needed for the open pool and for the draft_depth tokens a rollback can take back into a closed one. Unknown when the layers' pool ratios differ

one state per layer and the convolution windows, with the inputs of the draft_depth tokens a rollback takes back (a window row, a gate and a beta each), not a state apiece. Assumes rollback by replay: its time cost is derived, not measured, and a design that keeps one window plane per token (the 2026-11-14 plan) frees less (318 of 333 MiB at 128k)

rows.formula: 0 if draft_depth == 0 else ubatch * streams * n_embd * act_elem_bytes
rows.why: the draft reads the hidden rows of the tokens the last pass decoded, one ubatch at a time: a draft that takes the whole batch at once needs a batch of rows

rows.formula: max((1 + draft_depth) * vocab, ubatch * ceil(context / pool)) * act_elem_bytes
rows.rest: the floor is the largest single result a pass makes: a step's logits, or one ubatch's indexer scores over every pooled key (the term that grows with context). The engine's graph sets the rest: the batch it reserves for, a mask or converted copy of the cache, split copies of weights kept off the device, allocator reuse. Read the engine's reserve line at the placement used
